catalog_quote: Selayarese stress in monomorphemic words is normally penultimate, regardless of syllable structure: (1) a. sampúlo 'ten' b. palóla 'eggplant' c. balíka 'arm' d. barámba× 'chest' d. kalihára 'ant' e. kalumánti 'big black ant' f. búla× 'moon, month' g. tímbo 'grow' h. gónti× 'scissors' The sole exception involves monomorphemic words with antepenultimate stress: (2) a. sáhala /sahal/ 'profit' (cf. sahála /sahala/ 'sea cucumber') b. lámbere /lamber/ 'long' c. bótoro /botor/ 'gamble' ... In all monomorphemes with antepenultimate stress, the final vowel is absent before a vowel-initial, non-clitic suffix ...: (3) a. lámbere lambéra× /lamber+a×/ 'long/longer' ... Furthermore, all monomorphemic forms with antepenultimate stress end in V-r/l/s-V, where the two final vowels are identical. These forms have thus been analyzed as derived from stems ending in r,l, or s via epenthesis of a vowel which…

audit.reasoning: Quote check: both the main quote (Broselow 1999 ROA-334 sect. 2, pp.1-2) and the domain quote (Broselow p2k ms sect. 4.1 p.1) are verbatim in the held text layers at the stated locators. The coding (weight-blind penultimate in the prosodic word; suffixes inside, enclitics outside; closed lexical class of antepenultimate forms with final echo vowel after r/l/s) is stated identically in five held papers, including one co-authored by the native-speaker linguist Hasan Basri (Basri, Broselow & Finer, 'End of the Word in Makassar Languages', sect. 2.3) and Finer 1999 / Basri & Chen 1999 (TWPL 16). The deciding source is a 1999 theoretical phonology article rather than the primary description; the two primary works (Mithun & Basri 1986, 45 pp; Basri 1999 PhD, 371 pp) are not held and not open (JSTOR/ProQuest; Crossref and Semantic Scholar records
